title: Counterfactual Outcome Notes Coverage
dataSources: Forecasts (`prediction:forecast`), resolved outcomes (`prediction:outcome`), personal bets (`bet:personal`), calibration scores (`calibration:score`), Brier scores (`brier:score`).
app: Personal forecasting and calibration — a private prediction journal of dated forecasts about your own life, resolved outcomes, and calibration / Brier scoring — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=prediction:outcome
| stats sum(eval(if(counterfactual_note="yes",1,0))) as annotated, count as resolved by topic
| eval coverage_pct=round(100*annotated/resolved,1)
| sort - coverage_pct
description: Shows how often resolved forecasts include a short counterfactual note about what could have changed the outcome.
value: Counterfactual notes sharpen learning because they connect the result to the mechanism, not just the score.
implementation: Add a `counterfactual_note` flag to resolved outcomes and calculate coverage percentage by topic.
visualization: Table of topics with counterfactual note coverage.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces how often you write down what might have changed the outcome so you learn more than just right or wrong.
